answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable deposit that vests like a glacier: funds trickle back only after weeks of verified honest work, so creating a thousand fake agents means freezing a thousand deposits at once. Like a river carving a single channel through jade-hard rock, the slow release makes bulk identity farming unprofitable - an attacker pays the full time-value of capital per identity, while honest agents recover their bond and keep working.
